codeReview.summary: Well-structured implementation that closely follows the existing scrutiny.ts pattern. The behavioral validation prompt builder correctly handles first-run and re-validation modes, assertion collection from phases' fulfills fields is properly filtered by milestone and completion status, and the updateAssertionStatuses utility does atomic read-modify-write with proper error handling. All 33 tests pass covering prompt content, re-validation filtering, assertion collection, state updates, and routing. Two non-blocking observations noted.

issues.description: When building ContractAssertion objects from assertion IDs, title is set to the raw ID and description is a generic 'Verify assertion {id} from the validation contract.' This means the behavioral validation prompt does NOT contain the actual behavioral descriptions, titles, or evidence types from validation-contract.md — the worker must read the contract file during execution to get these. While this works (the worker is instructed to read the contract), it makes the prompt less self-contained than the Droid reference implementation, where the user-testing-validator parses the contract and includes assertion details in the prompt. The test suite's assertions pass because the test fixtures provide full ContractAssertion objects directly, masking this gap in the production integration path.

The stage-loop-factory routing tests (lines 455-477) are purely structural — they test string prefix matching ('Validation: '.startsWith) in isolation rather than exercising the actual promptBuilder callback in stage-loop-factory.ts. This means a regression in the factory wiring (e.g., the if-condition being removed or reordered) would not be caught by these tests. The scrutiny validation tests have the same limitation, so this is consistent with existing patterns but worth noting.

The worker must read the contract file independently. Tests mask this because they provide full ContractAssertion objects directly.

Stage-loop-factory routing tests verify string prefix matching in isolation rather than the actual factory callback, consistent with the existing scrutiny test pattern but not catching potential factory wiring regressions.

sharedStateObservations.observation: AGENTS.md does not document the 'Validation:' phase title prefix convention or the behavioral validation prompt routing. The 'Scrutiny:' prefix is only implicitly documented via the validation-phase-auto-injection feature. Adding a note about validation phase title prefixes (Scrutiny: and Validation:) and their routing in stage-loop-factory would help future workers understand the convention.

The architecture.md library file documents the Validation Contract and State section but does not mention the behavioral validation prompt or the Validation: prefix routing in stage-loop-factory. It would benefit from a note about the three validation phase types (Scrutiny, Behavioral Validation, End-of-Session Gate) and how they are routed.

summary: PASS. The behavioral validation phase implementation is correct, well-tested (33 tests, all passing), follows existing codebase patterns (mirrors scrutiny.ts structure), and properly integrates with the stage-loop-factory prompt routing. The updateAssertionStatuses utility in validation-state.ts correctly handles atomic state updates with proper Zod validation. Two non-blocking issues noted: (1) production ContractAssertion objects lack real contract data (titles/descriptions are generic, worker must read contract file), and (2) factory routing tests are structural rather than integration-level. Both are consistent with existing patterns and do not block.
